title: Robotics Day Sparks Ideas for Accessible, Purposeful Design
summary: A visit to Purdue Robotics Day prompted new questions about robots for learning, care, and companionship.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post

paragraphs.text: Chorong Park reflected on a recent Robotics Day visit in an April 6, 2026, post, describing encounters with projects that opened up new directions for human-robot interaction. Her photographs capture a range of demonstrations and exhibits.

The visit prompted questions about designing robots for specific everyday purposes, including education, healthcare, and companionship for older adults. Park emphasized that well-being and accessibility should guide those design decisions.

She thanked Rua M. Williams, Anastasia Kouvaras Ostrowski, and Sooyeon Jeong for sharing research and projects during the visit. The exchange offered a chance to connect technical possibilities with questions about genuine human connection.
Looking ahead to CHI 2026, Park expressed interest in continuing those conversations. The post records a research exchange and emerging ideas, rather than new clinical findings or a product launch.
